title: CILIARY DYSKINESIA, PRIMARY, 2
alt_titles: CILIARY DYSKINESIA, PRIMARY, 2, WITH OR WITHOUT SITUS INVERSUS

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that primary ciliary dyskinesia-2 (CILD2) is caused by homozygous mutation in the DNAAF3 gene (614566) on chromosome 19q13.

checks.claim: Primary ciliary dyskinesia-2 (CILD2) is caused by homozygous mutation in the DNAAF3 gene.

checks.explanation: Homozygous DNAAF3 mutations in CILD2-linked families.

checks.claim: The DNAAF3 gene is located on chromosome 19q13.
checks.evidence_quote: The human DAB1 orthologous gene DNAAF3 on human chromosome 19q13 (previously designated C19orf51) encodes a 588 amino acid protein

paragraphs.text: Meeks et al. (2000) described primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) as an autosomal recessive condition with chronic sinusitis, bronchiectasis, and subfertility. They reported that situs inversus occurs in 50% of cases (Kartagener syndrome) and that the estimated incidence is 1 in 20,000 live births. They stated that the disorder is caused by defective ciliary function with ultrastructural abnormalities, including absent dynein arms, absent radial spokes, and disturbed ciliary orientation.

checks.evidence_quote: Primary ciliary dyskinesia is an autosomal recessive condition

checks.evidence_quote: characterised by chronic sinusitis, bronchiectasis, and subfertility

checks.claim: Situs inversus occurs in 50% of primary ciliary dyskinesia cases (Kartagener syndrome).
checks.evidence_quote: Situs inversus occurs in 50% of cases (Kartagener syndrome).

checks.claim: The estimated incidence of primary ciliary dyskinesia is 1 in 20,000 live births.
checks.evidence_quote: It has an estimated incidence of 1 in 20 000 live births.

checks.evidence_quote: The clinical phenotype is caused by defective ciliary function

checks.evidence_quote: associated with a range of ultrastructural abnormalities including absent dynein arms, absent radial spokes, and disturbed ciliary orientation

paragraphs.text: Mitchison et al. (2012) studied 10 patients with PCD from 3 consanguineous families: 2 families of Arabic origin and a UK-Pakistani first-cousin family. The patients had neonatal respiratory distress, recurrent cough and wheezing, nasal discharge, chest infections, sinusitis, otitis media, nasal polyps, and bronchiectasis. Four of the 10 had situs inversus. Electron microscopy showed reduced or absent inner and outer dynein arms. Nasal cilia were immotile in all affected individuals. The authors noted that the disorder was associated with male infertility.

paragraphs.text: Meeks et al. (2000) performed a genome scan in 5 Arabic families with primary ciliary dyskinesia. Using GENEHUNTER, they obtained a maximal multipoint lod score (HLOD) of 4.4 on chromosome 19q13.3-qter at alpha (proportion of linked families) = 0.7. Recombinations at D19S572 and D19S218 defined a 15-cM critical region.

This locus had been mapped in consanguineous Arabic-origin PCD families with immotile cilia and absent outer dynein arms. In 2 of the 3 originally linked families, affected individuals showed large regions of marker homozygosity across the DNAAF3 locus.

paragraphs.text: Mitchison et al. (2012) also found a homozygous c.973G-A variant in the DNAAF3 gene, resulting in an ala325-to-thr (A325T) substitution, in a Belgian patient with PCD. paragraphs.text: Using immunofluorescence, Mitchison et al. (2012) found that the outer dynein arm components DNAH5, DNAH9, and DNAI2 and the inner dynein arm light chain DNALI1 were absent from respiratory cilia of patients with DNAAF3 mutations. In some patients, residual DNAH5 and DNALI1 were present in the apical cytoplasm. These findings suggested that DNAAF3 is required for cytoplasmic preassembly of outer and inner dynein arms along the entire axoneme.

checks.claim: The immunofluorescence findings of Mitchison et al. (2012) suggested that DNAAF3 is required for cytoplasmic preassembly of outer and inner dynein arms along the entire axoneme.

checks.explanation: The paper concludes from immunofluorescence that DNAAF3 is needed for assembly along the entire axoneme; the 'cytoplasmic preassembly' role is drawn from other parts of the paper, not from these findings.

paragraphs.text: Mitchison et al. (2012) studied the Chlamydomonas pf22 mutant, which carries a nonsense mutation (trp79-to-ter; W79X) in the DNAAF3 ortholog. The mutant had paralyzed half-length flagella lacking outer dynein arms and inner dynein arms b and c. PF22 was found exclusively in the cytoplasm. In pf22 cytoplasm, IC2 was hyperabundant and heavy chain-intermediate chain complexes formed abnormally. These findings suggested that PF22 acts at a later step of dynein preassembly than PF13 and ODA7.

paragraphs.text: Mitchison et al. (2012) found that morpholino knockdown of dnaaf3 in zebrafish caused immotile olfactory placode cilia with reduced or missing dynein arms. Morphant embryos also showed body axis curvature, hydrocephalus, pronephric cysts, otolith defects, and left-right patterning defects. About half of dnaaf3MOex8 embryos had reversed or absent heart looping.
